Finance · Ignore missed days — mockups

1 · The question: how does an admin ignore missed days?

Why

Jeffrey (2026-10-28): “I don’t want error messages to pile up. Have a seen message or ignore it … ignore the missed days so we don’t see them again, basically saying we saw it, accept it, and want to ignore it.” Today History’s amber line lists every day this month that wasn’t closed (22 in the preview) and grows every day nobody closes.

This builds on v0.811’s rejected option C (“mark days ‘Won’t be closed’ in History — needs a migration; can be added later”, drawn in TKD-Finance-DailyReport-Questions.html #q17 with a reason note “Before Finance was used”). The new rulebook row would change v0.811; its OK button stays.

Where a missed day shows up today (all checked in the code)

  • History (admins only): the amber line “22 days this month weren’t closed: …” and an amber Not closed tag on each such row. The database decides: a day with counted payments (or refunds), before today, with no close in force (finance_history, 0011). Days with no payments, or only returned checks, never count.
  • Home (admins only): “25 earlier days at Worcester weren’t closed, the first on Mon, Sep 28.” — the last 30 days, so it spans two months (finance_home_at). Its OK (v0.811) is remembered on that device only and doesn’t touch History.
  • Both: a school’s box says gray “Not closed yet”. Print: “Not closed yet”.
  • The day’s own Daily report says nothing — only the “Close the day…” button shows.
  • Staff never see earlier days (v0.806); their “Today’s drawer isn’t closed yet” is about today only.

Option A · a button on History’s amber line

  • The button repeats the count: Ignore 22 days invented (phones: under the words). It opens the shared “are you sure?” box; its action says the same words, blue, first focus on the action (nothing is lost for good: v1.008 / v1.103, loses='nothing').
  • The line goes away; those rows say gray Ignored. A later missed day brings the line back with just that day.
  • Undo one day: open it, Stop ignoring (section 4).
  • + One press clears the pile. + Smallest change. − Keeping one day flagged takes two steps (ignore all, then Stop ignoring on that day).

Option B · “Ignore this day” on each day’s report

  • A missed earlier day gets an amber line on its report, “This day wasn’t closed.” invented, with Ignore this day invented (no “are you sure?”; Stop ignoring undoes it). History’s line only counts days not ignored.
  • + Each day is a deliberate choice. − 22 days = 22 opens and 22 presses: the pile stays until someone clicks through it.

Option C · both

  • + Clear the pile in one press, or ignore one day. − Two ways to do one thing; the extra per-day button is rarely needed, since A plus Stop ignoring covers it.

Recommendation: A. It is what Jeffrey asked for: one “we saw it” press. Separately, a small extra (section 3): the day’s report says “This day wasn’t closed.” — without a button. Choose C only if you want to ignore single days from their report.

Amber outline (#d97706) = what changes; “Now” pictures have none. All pictures are the real preview app (fake data, Worcester, today Wed, Oct 28, 2026) with the new parts drawn on top. History pictures (Now and After) show the approved “← Back to the day” text link (v0.820; approved, not built yet), so it isn’t a difference here.

2 · Which days does “Ignore” take? (follows from A)

History’s line is one month (22 October days here). Home’s line is the last 30 days (25 = 22 October + 3 September). Worcester has 28 unclosed earlier days in all (6 in September).

  • S1 · The days the line lists (this month, the school chosen; on Both, both schools). Home then still says “3 earlier days at Worcester weren’t closed, the first on Mon, Sep 28.”; Open History goes to September, where one more press clears them. + You ignore only days you see (“we saw it”). − Older months need their own press, once.
  • S2 · Every earlier unclosed day at this school, all months: the button says Ignore all 28 days invented and the box names the months (“22 in October, 6 in September”) invented. Home’s line is gone at once. + One press, everything. − It ignores days that aren’t on the screen.

Recommendation: S1 — matches “we saw it, accept it”; the extra September press happens once, while catching up.

The confirm box

Home afterwards (Home skips ignored days in both)

Home’s line counts only days not ignored, on every admin device. OK (v0.811) stays for “not now” on this device, and its “N new … (21 seen before)” wording also skips ignored days. No Ignore button on Home (proposal): it is a money decision, made in History with the days in front of you.

3 · Small extra: the day’s report says it wasn’t closed

Today an earlier unclosed day’s report says nothing. Proposal (with A): an amber line under the date row, “This day wasn’t closed.” invented, no button. With C the same line carries “Ignore this day” (section 1, option B picture). Admins only — staff never see earlier days.

4 · What an ignored day looks like

  • History: gray Ignored invented tag (gray like “No payments”: nothing to act on), and the Closed by column says “Ignored by Jeffrey Berg · Oct 28” invented (tablet and phones: a second line, like “Closed by …”). The amber line counts only days not ignored, and is gone when there are none.
  • The day’s report (any option): a Day ignored invented box where the Day closed box would be: “Not closed. Jeffrey Berg ignored it on Wed, Oct 28 at 4:20 PM.” invented and Stop ignoring invented (no icon) with “It then counts as not closed again.” invented Box icon ti-eye-off (new in the icon map; ti-eye is already Preview, v0.235, so Stop ignoring has none).
  • Close the day… still works on an ignored day (proposal): closing wins and the day becomes Closed.
  • Print (not drawn): the count line says “Not closed · ignored by Jeffrey Berg on Oct 28” invented instead of “Not closed yet”.
  • Payments, totals and Export don’t change (the export file has no closing column). Who ignored which day and when is kept and logged.

5 · A day comes back if its money changes after it was ignored (proposal)

  • Like “Changed after closing” (v0.199): the database remembers the day’s payments when it was ignored. If a payment is later added, undone, edited or moved on that day, the day stops being ignored: Not closed again, back in History’s line and on Home. New money is a new thing to look at.
  • The report says why, in Changed after closing’s words: “This day wasn’t closed. 1 payment changed after it was ignored: 1 added on Wed at 5:25 PM, so it shows again.” invented The new payment’s row says gray “Added after ignoring” invented with “Recorded Wed, Oct 28 at 5:25 PM, after the day was ignored” invented (like “Added after closing”).
  • Drawn for A (+ the small extra): the line has no button; with C it would carry “Ignore this day”.
  • Alternative: once ignored, always ignored (simpler database; a late payment on an ignored day goes unnoticed).

6 · Both: Worcester’s and Shrewsbury’s boxes say Ignored (proposal)

On an earlier day, a school box that would say gray “Not closed yet” says gray Ignored invented when that school’s day is ignored (Mon, Oct 26 here, both schools’ days ignored).

7 · Who can do it, and the database work

Who

  • Admins only, enforced in the database (History and earlier days are admin-only already, v0.806; staff never see earlier days). Only days before today that weren’t closed; today never (it has its own reminder). Stop ignoring: admins too.

What it needs in the database (plain words — no SQL written yet)

  • A new append-only record: school, day, “ignore” or “stop ignoring”, who (name + login id, never shown), when, and a fingerprint of the day’s payments (for section 5). Nothing changed or deleted; Stop ignoring is a new row pointing at the ignore. RLS on, no direct rights for the app, every row in change_log.
  • Two new admin-only write functions (security definer, has_data_access() first): ignore days (a list of school + day, with what the screen saw, so a day closed or changed meanwhile is refused as “stale”) and stop ignoring.
  • Changed read functions: finance_history (tag “ignored”, who / when; the count skips it), finance_home_at (skips ignored days), finance_day (the ignore and “changed after it was ignored”), finance_day_both (Ignored in a box). Rebuilt from the live 0011 / 0026 versions with a guard like 0026.
  • So: a migration (number from Main — next free is 0032), PGlite tests, a security review, your paste, then the screens + the preview’s fake database. Nothing applied or deployed without your OK.

8 · Smaller questions (proposals — OK together or one by one)

  1. Scope — S1, the days the line lists (section 2).
  2. The small extra — the report says “This day wasn’t closed.”, no button (section 3).
  3. The word — Ignored (your word), or v0.811’s Won’t be closed (says what it means for the drawer; longer on phones). Recommended: Ignored.
  4. A note when ignoring? — v0.811’s option C had a reason box (“Before Finance was used”, shown in History). Recommended: no note; name and time are kept, and a box slows the one-press clear. Alternative: an optional note in the confirm box.
  5. Comes back when the money changes — yes (section 5).
  6. Home skips ignored days; OK stays; no Ignore on Home (section 2).
  7. Closing an ignored day still allowed — yes; Closed wins.
  8. Print — “Not closed · ignored by Jeffrey Berg on Oct 28”.
  9. The wording marked invented.
